leading_positions.synthesis: Four files give B020 as the preferred single-part prize, each with Helpman and Melitz. The shared case is that firm heterogeneity and selection moved trade analysis from industries to firms, changed empirical practice and quantitative policy evaluation, and has more than two decades of replication behind it. The supporters also share the main reservation: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not on the credited list, and Helpman's overlap with B001 forces a choice about which body of his work is recognised. They differ on Redding. Strömberg regards a third seat as arguable, while Friberg and Boppart treat Redding's work as a later extension. Citation wording differs slightly (productivity and gains from trade; welfare gains; pattern of trade). The supporters do not say whether the credit gap would be disqualifying, and Boppart holds his view with moderate confidence. Andersson, Hjalmarsson and Teorell name or discuss B020 as an alternative or serious rival, but their preferred prize is B001.

Three files give B001 (Grossman and Helpman) as the preferred prize. They share three points: the pair is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, the work is fully mature, and protection for sale plus the trade-innovation-growth models form a durable framework. They also share the main reservation, that empirical support for protection-for-sale predictions is mixed, so the case rests on framework influence rather than settled confirmation. Their emphasis differs. Andersson stresses mechanism-style generality and the unresolved B020 credit boundary, Hjalmarsson distinguishes contested magnitudes from no lasting contribution, and Teorell wants the case to stand on B001 alone and not on Helpman's B020 credit. B001 is named as an alternative in eight round-1 files (Boppart, Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Friberg, Hassler, Krusell, Strömberg), but an alternative is not a first-choice preference and is not counted as support. Friberg, for example, says he could accept B001 but argues B020 is stronger on empirical confirmation.

Three files give B016 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) as the preferred prize. All propose the same three names and frame the citation around a research programme on electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity, not on any single estimate. Common reservations are weaker identification for constitutional and electoral-rule effects, thematic proximity to the 2024 institutions prize, and credit that cannot be cleanly separated between the Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson strands. The supporters argue that B016 differs from the 2024 prize in subject (rules and fiscal outcomes versus long-run historical origins). Krusell holds first place with moderate confidence and calls B001 the closest rival. Fredriksson ranks B016 first while saying B019 has better identification in its best designs. Because the chair is one of the three supporters and Krusell notes that agreement with Hassler is not independent evidence, the three files should not be read as three independent assessments.

One file gives B019 as the preferred prize, with Autor, Hanson and Dorn credited for empirical analysis of adjustment to trade and technological change. The case rests on transparent, heavily re-analysed quasi-experimental designs and on a finding of slow, geographically concentrated adjustment that Dreber regards as robust to the main critiques. She deliberately keeps the citation off the wider task-based theory literature. Her own caveats are the continuing debate over magnitude, persistence and shift-share validity, and the Dorn-versus-Katz choice. Other files engage with this candidate: Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson and Teorell name it as an alternative, Boppart prefers Katz as the third name, and Andersson ranked it seventh at the opening stage.

areas_of_agreement: Every round-1 file proposes a single-part prize, and no member proposes crediting Helpman in two parts. Andersson, Boppart and Friberg state explicitly that the Committee should choose between the two Helpman strands rather than combine them.

The B001 and B020 supporters concede each other's main weakness: B020 supporters accept that B001 has the cleaner attribution, and B001 supporters accept that its empirical support is mixed and that B020's footprint in data and estimation is wider. The dispute is about weighting, not about these facts.

Members who discuss it agree that the absence of a trade prize since 2008 is a field-balance consideration, not scientific merit, and that it applies equally to B001 and B020 (Andersson, Enflo, Friberg, Teorell).
B001, B016 and B020 are described as mature, with no timing concern, in the files that discuss them.

Supporters and critics of B016 agree that identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects is weaker than in design-based candidates, and that overlap with the 2024 institutions prize is the main risk to that candidate.

On B031, the members who address attribution prefer the two-name Kiyotaki-Moore version to adding Gertler (Boppart, Strömberg, and Krusell, who opened with Gertler as a third name). The main concern is overlap with the 2022 prize.
scientific_disputes: B001 versus B020: whether conceptual and organising influence on theory (protection for sale, trade-innovation-growth) should weigh as much as measurable consequences for data use, estimation and quantitative policy evaluation (firm heterogeneity). Hjalmarsson argues that mixed test results are normal for a testable framework and are not evidence of failure. Friberg, Strömberg and Enflo treat weaker empirical confirmation as a reason to rank B001 lower.
B020: how far the gains-from-trade results depend on parametric assumptions such as Pareto productivity and CES demand, and how much that should count against the empirical side of the case.

B016: whether a research programme with weaker identification, in which institutions are not randomly assigned, merits the same weight as design-based work. Hassler, Krusell and Fredriksson say the citation should rest on the framework and on later within-country designs. Teorell, Andersson and the supporters' own caveats treat this as a real weakness.

B016 and 2024: whether rules-to-fiscal-outcomes work is complementary to the 2024 prize or reduces marginal novelty. Andersson keeps B016 behind B001 partly on this ground, and the B016 supporters reject that reading.

B019: whether the magnitude and long-run persistence of the China-shock effects and the validity of shift-share exposure designs are settled enough for a prize. Dreber says the qualitative result is robust. Andersson and Hjalmarsson say the debate is still open. Dreber says she has not independently verified this.
Across candidates: how to weigh design-based credibility, framework breadth and cumulative field-building under a single common criterion.
attribution_disputes: B020: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not on the credited list. The four supporters regard Helpman and Melitz as the most defensible pair and propose wording centred on the mechanism. Teorell and Andersson treat the gap as a reason to rank B020 below B001, and Hjalmarsson cites it against B020. Redding's role is also unsettled: Strömberg sees a third seat as arguable, while Friberg and Boppart treat his work as later and more derivative.

B001: attribution is described as the cleanest on the shortlist. Andersson raises one unverified question about how much of the novelty lies in the application, given that the common-agency machinery came from earlier work, and the open framing question is Helpman's overlap with B020.

B016: credit cannot be cleanly split between Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson, and adjacent contributors (Alesina, deceased; Acemoglu and Robinson, recognised in 2024; Dixit) are outside the three-name set. Fredriksson and Hassler defend the trio as the cleanest cut of the specific contribution.

B019: laureate proposals differ. Dreber, Enflo, Hjalmarsson, Krusell and Teorell propose Autor, Hanson and Dorn, Andersson proposes Autor, Dorn and Hanson, Fredriksson and Friberg propose only Autor and Hanson, and Boppart proposes Autor, Katz and Hanson. Separate questions are whether the task framework has co-originators outside the credited set (including Acemoglu and Restrepo) and whether the trade-shock and task strands form one achievement.

B031 (not a first choice for anyone): Gertler as a third name remains a difference between Krusell's opening proposal and the two-name Kiyotaki-Moore versions, because the financial-accelerator strand overlaps with an existing laureate.
maturity_disputes: No file raises a maturity concern for B001, B016 or B020.

B019: Dreber regards the core papers as a decade or more old with no timing concern. Hjalmarsson notes that the China-shock papers date from 2013 onward and that long-run persistence is still debated.

Recency of earlier recognition is raised as a separate consideration from maturity: trade in 2008 (B001, B020), banks and financial crises in 2022 (B031), and institutions in 2024 (B016). Members differ on whether this bears on merit or only on field balance and marginal novelty.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: The chair (Hassler) prefers B016. His research on dynamic political economy (the welfare state, the dynamics of government) is thematically adjacent to B016, though his file reports no tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley. This summary should be read with that position disclosed.

Co-authorship among committee members who prefer different candidates: Hassler with Krusell, Boppart and Friberg; Friberg also reports a 2026 paper with Hassler and Ellingsen. Boppart's file notes co-authorship with Krusell and Hassler, who both prefer B016. Krusell notes that his agreement with Hassler should not count as independent evidence. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
Boppart discloses a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow, who is credited on shortlisted B036. B036 is not part of his configuration and no member prefers it.

Fredriksson, Krusell and Teorell mention possible Swedish-institutional proximity of some B016 candidates to the Committee. Teorell and Fredriksson also describe B016 as adjacent to their own fields or to the IIES macro group. No specific relationship to any candidate is stated or verified.

Friberg's research in industrial organisation and trade is thematically close to B020, B001 and B041. His file also notes his spouse's public political role as a public fact only, with no stated bearing on any candidate.

Collegial ties among committee members are disclosed (Andersson with Dreber, Friberg and Strömberg at SSE; Andersson and Enflo at Lund; Teorell with Hassler, Krusell and Boppart at Stockholm University). None is a link to a credited candidate. No file reports a co-authorship or institutional tie to any credited candidate on its preferred ballot item.
questions_for_round2: B020 supporters (Boppart, Enflo, Friberg, Strömberg): is the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum from the credited list disqualifying for a Helpman-Melitz award? If not, what citation wording would describe the mechanism without implying that the firm-level empirical literature is exhausted?

B001 supporters (Andersson, Hjalmarsson, Teorell): how should mixed empirical support for protection-for-sale predictions be weighed against framework influence, and what evidence of impact outside trade theory and political economy supports the case?

All members: if the Committee recognises trade, would you accept either B001 or B020 as a single-part award? If one is your clear second choice, state which, and state whether Helpman's role in both justifies a different framing.

B016 supporters (Fredriksson, Hassler, Krusell) and Andersson and Teorell: does a citation limited to electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity in fiscal policy separate B016 from the 2024 prize enough to resolve the overlap concern? Can the three-name set be justified without the Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson strands being separable?

Dreber and Fredriksson: should a B019 citation credit Autor, Hanson and Dorn on China-shock evidence, or only Autor and Hanson? If a third name, what evidence decides between Dorn and Katz, and does the Acemoglu-Restrepo overlap affect the task-framework strand?

All members: since B016, B001, B019 and B020 differ in how far identification quality, framework breadth and cumulative field-building carry weight, can the Committee state one common weighting that each member can apply to all four candidates?

Members who named B031 as an alternative (Boppart, Hassler, Krusell, Strömberg): does the 2022 prize leave enough marginal case for Kiyotaki and Moore to compete with the four candidates above, and would Gertler be added or excluded?
summary.chair_observation: Round-1 first preferences are split 4/3/3/1 across B020, B001, B016 and B019, so no candidate has the six explicit first-choice preferences a majority needs. B001 and B020 share Helpman but differ in the other laureate and in the citation, so their first-choice counts should not be added together. B001 is the only candidate that appears in every file, as a first choice for three and an alternative for eight; this describes the written positions, not hidden votes. The disputes do not run along field lines. Members who rank different candidates first often cite the same strengths and the same weaknesses. B001 has the cleanest attribution but mixed empirical support, B020 has the widest empirical footprint but an unresolved credit boundary, and B016 has the broadest programme but weaker identification and 2024 overlap. Disclosed ties among members are noted without adjudication, and the chair's own B016 preference is among the positions summarised here.
